glosses: disrespectful

examples.text: Die Respektlosen, die ich über mein indogermanisches Erbe und meine Vorfahren gesagt, gedacht und getan habe, sind null und nichtig.
examples.translation: The disrespectful things, that I said, thought, and did about my Indo-European heritage and ancestors, are null and void.
examples.english: The disrespectful things, that I said, thought, and did about my Indo-European heritage and ancestors, are null and void.

glosses: непочтительный, неуважительный
bez szacunku, lekceważący
bez szacunku, lekceważąco
Irrespectueux, qui manque de respect.

examples.text: (Mein Chef) ist respektlos den Mitarbeitern gegenüber, nutzt Meetings, um sich stundenlang bei mir über die Welt zu beschweren… Ich kann es nicht länger ertragen.
examples.translation: (Mon supérieur) manque de respect à ses collaborateurs, profite des réunions pour se plaindre du monde pendant des heures auprès de moi... Je ne peux plus le supporter.

examples.text: Am Donnerstag wurde auch Richard Barnett, der sich demonstrativ respektlos mit dem Fuß auf dem Schreibtisch im Büro der damaligen Repräsentantenhauschefin Nancy Pelosi hatte ablichten lassen, zu vier Jahren Haft verurteilt.
examples.translation: Jeudi, Richard Barnett, qui s’était fait photographier de manière ostensiblement irrespectueuse, le pied posé sur le bureau dans le bureau de Nancy Pelosi, alors présidente de la Chambre des représentants, a également été condamné à quatre ans de prison.

glosses: ohne Respekt

examples.text: Sein respektloses Verhalten gegenüber dem Lehrer hatte Konsequenzen.
„Ein Kunde einer Pizzeria dürfte einen gehörigen Schock erlebt haben, als sein Blick auf den Kassenzettel fiel: Ein Angestellter des Restaurants hatte darauf respektlose Worte hinterlassen.“
„Double-Gewinner Niko Kovac vom FC Bayern München hat einen respektlosen Umgang mit den Fußball-Trainern in der Bundesliga beklagt.“

„Über Trumps respektlosen Umgang mit verheirateten Frauen hat auch Trumps ehemalige Geschäftspartnerin Jill Harth berichtet, die über einen längeren Zeitraum von ihm sexuell belästigt worden sein soll.“
„Diskus-Olympiasieger Christoph Harting hat nach seinen respektlosen Äußerungen und herablassenden Sprüchen über Verband und Konkurrenten offenbar einen Denkzettel erhalten.“

glosses: Lacking respect.
irrespective, heedless, regardless

examples.text: That alone, apart from Mr. Wyse’s old-fashioned notions on the subject, made telephoning impossible, for your summons was usually answered by his cook, who instantly began scolding the butcher irrespective and disrespectful of whom you were.

glosses: In a disrespectful manner; with a lack of respect.

examples.text: As a matter of fact its narrow ornate façade presented not a single quiet space that the eyes might rest on after a tiring attempt to follow and codify the arabesques, foliations, and intricate vermiculations of what some disrespectfully dubbed as “near-aissance.”
She became disrespectfully referred to locally as the "Crab" on account of her extraordinary manoeuvrability.

glosses: Showing disregard, indicating rejection, serving to dismiss.

examples.text: I was openly dismissive about transubstantiation, by which the host is consecrated, and according to Catholic doctrine, literally turns from mere bread into the body of Christ. “But all the atoms stay the same!” I would insist. “That makes no sense!”

glosses: Lacking respect; not having or not showing respect for or seriousness towards something that is usually treated with respect; going against conventional precepts.

examples.text: an irreverent new work
an irreverent examination of reviewing
Beyond the hut a clump of myalls loomed spectral and wraith-like, and round them a gang of crows cawed noisily, irreverent of the great silence.

glosses: Showing disrespect through a casual attitude, levity, and a lack of due seriousness; pert.

examples.text: a sort of flippant, vain discourse
The conversations had grown more adult over the years—she was less flippant, at least.
In the mid-1950s we both wrote for the same weekly, where her contributions were a good deal more serious and less flippant than mine.
Our society treats smoking flippantly as a slightly distasteful habit that can injure your health. It is not. It is drug addiction.

glosses: Loquacious; speaking with ease and rapidity.

examples.text:
November 5, 1673, Isaac Barrow, sermon on the Gunpowder Treason
It becometh good men, in such cases, to be pleasantly flippant and free in their speech.

glosses: Nimble; limber.
Not respectful.

examples.text: The character, however, of which the assumed name is truly expressive, deserves from us no unrespectful attention; we shall best possess our readers of it by laying before them one or two passages from the preface.

This, supported by Whalley and Goffe, calmed the meeting somewhat; and, after much more speaking, in which the necessity of a separation of the military power from the civil was a prominent topic, the result was "A Humble Representation and Petition of the Officers of the Armies of England, Scotland, and Ireland," expressed in general and not unrespectful terms, but conveying sufficiently the Army's demands.

glosses: In a way that is not respectful.
Not befitting or proper for a son.
Not pious.
Lacking reverence or respect, especially towards a god.

examples.text: […] surfaces too great to belong to anything right or proper for this earth, and impious with horrible images and hieroglyphs.

glosses: In an irreverent manner.

examples.text: He finds out, soon enough for his weal and his bane, that he is stronger than Nature: and right tyrannously and irreverently he lords it over her, clearing, delving, dyking, building, without fear or shame.
Elisha […] was able to call upon two she-bears to come and eat up the children who had treated him irreverently […]

glosses: In an unfilial manner.
Qui s'oppose à son supérieur, hiérarchique ou autre, de façon moqueuse ; qui perd le respect à force d’effronterie ou de hardiesse excessive.

examples.text: Un élève insolent.
Pour la troisième fois, et sur un ton intolérablement agressif, il réitéra son insolente question. Un silence gros de danger suivit.

glosses: Celui qui offense la modestie, la pudeur, qui manque aux égards, aux convenances.

examples.text: Il est insolent, fort insolent avec les femmes.

glosses: Qui en use avec orgueil, avec dureté.

examples.text: Il ne faut pas être insolent dans la victoire, dans la bonne fortune.
La prospérité l’a rendu insolent.
Les airs insolents, le ton insolent d’un parvenu.
Cet ordre insolent les irrita.

glosses: Insolite. On dit encore « bonheur insolent », « fortune insolente », « chance insolente », en parlant d’un bonheur, d’une fortune, d’une chance extraordinaire.

examples.text: Les Grangers avaient encore contre eux ceci qu’en un grand nombre de circonstances ils semblaient favorisés par une chance qui était au moins insolente pour les camarades.

glosses: Celui qui est insolent.

examples.text: C’est un insolent.
Vous êtes un insolent, s’écria avec emportement Eugène, vous méritez une correction et vous la recevrez.
